title: Though to Swallow: A Rare Case of Esophageal Tuberculosis
case_text:
A 29-year-old Ghana male who had immigrated 2 years prior to presentation with past medical history of GERD presented to the emergency department with the complaints of retrosternal chest pain and odynophagia of 6 months duration. His symptoms seemed to be accelerating in the last 3 weeks. The acceleration of his symptoms also coincided with the development of fever and nocturnal hyperhidrosis. He noted an approximate 6.8 kg weight loss in the preceding months. Routine and specialized laboratory studies were obtained and were notable for the following: white blood cell count of 5.37, CD4+ of 22, positive HIV fourth generation screen, negative for AFB sputum X3, IGRA positive, Negative for fungal panel, and positive for Toxoplasma and CMV IgG but negative for IgM. CTA chest showed soft tissue thickening in the subcarinal region extending into the AP window being suspicious for a mass/adenopathy with primary differential consideration including lymphoma. CT Abdomen and pelvis was then done to show multiple sub-centimeter hypodense lesions in the spleen. The patient then underwent EGD which found an esophageal ulcer, surgical pathology of the esophageal ulcer showed acute and chronic granulations tissue but negative for CMV, HSV and AFB stains. Later, he underwent a subsequent EUS guided FNA of the subcarinal lymph nodes and splenic lesions. Surgical pathology showed necrotizing granulomas, Scant fragments of necrotic material with histiocytes, blood and fibrin mixed with scant lymphocytes, AFB and GMS stains were negative for microorganisms and could not specify the actual organism. The patient was started on ATT therapy including INH, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol in addition to azithromycin to cover for MAC mycobacteria. but once we received the culture report of the sputum which was sent three weeks ago on admission showing positivity for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, we discontinued azithromycin and continued ATT. To avoid IRIS (Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome) we started HAART therapy 2 weeks after starting ATT.
No evidence of pulmonary embolism.
Significant soft tissue thickening in the subcarinal region extending into the AP window and precarinal region. Findings are suspicious for a mass/adenopathy with primary differential consideration including lymphoma. Metastatic disease is a differential diagnostic consideration. Soft tissue surrounds the esophagus although primary esophageal cancer is considered less likely. Clinical correlation recommended.
Indeterminate 4 mm nodule right lower lobe. Follow-up is recommended to ensure long-term stability.
Although the spleen is not enlarged, there are multiple low-density lesions measuring less than 1 cm scattered throughout the spleen. Appearance can be seen with lymphoma/leukemia or metastatic disease.
There is a 1.6 cm low-density area adjacent to the distal esophagus and liver which appears external to the liver and likely reflects a prominent periesophageal/mediastinal lymph node.
The Z-line was regular and was found 37 cm from the incisors. One cratered deep esophageal ulcer no stigmata of recent bleeding was found in the middle third of the esophagus. The lesion was 23 mm in largest dimension. This was biopsied with a cold forceps for histology for CMV, HSV and TB.
- One cratered deep esophageal ulcer no stigmata of recent bleeding was found in the middle third of the esophagus.
- Three abnormal lymph nodes were visualized in the subcarinal mediastinum (level 7).
Fine needle aspiration performed.
- Four abnormal lymph nodes were visualized in the celiac region (level 20) and peri-gastric region.
Fine needle aspiration performed.
- Multiple hypoechoic lesions were found in the spleen. Fine needle aspiration performed.

   - Do NOT invent, embellish, or smooth out missing clinical data.
   - Never extrapolate findings not explicitly mentioned.

2. THE ADMISSION BREAKPOINT PRINCIPLE (CRITICAL):
   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Tuberculosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: esophageal tuberculosis and HIV infection
